claude_proposed_widenings.name: grant_spellcasting (ClassFeatureMechanics family)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Spellcasting is a passive infrastructure grant, not an activated feature. The existing 'activation' family requires an activation cost, a use_count resource with a cap, and a single effect from {grant_extra_action, heal_hp}. None of these map honestly to a feature that passively grants a spell slot table, cantrip pool, prepared spell list, spellcasting ability designation, and focus permission.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. [...] Spell Slots. The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest. [...] Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. [...] Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Druid spells.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: spell_slot_table resource (multi-level, class-level-scaled)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Druid spell slots are a two-dimensional resource: indexed by spell slot level (1–9) AND scaled by class level per a class-specific table. UseCountResource models a single integer cap, optionally tiered by class level. It cannot express a pool of distinct slot levels each with their own count, all resetting on Long Rest.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: cantrip_pool (known-cantrip count scaling by class level with threshold_tiers)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The cantrip pool is a known-spell count (not slots) that starts at 2 and gains +1 at class levels 4 and 10. This is a threshold_tiers<number> scaled by the 'class' axis. No existing ClassFeatureEffect variant models 'grants N known cantrips from a spell list, scaling by class level.' The v4 atom grant_spell_access exists but has no corresponding ClassFeatureEffect variant.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You know two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. [...] When you reach Druid levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: prepared_spell_list (prepared-spell count scaling by class level, Long Rest changeable)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Prepared spells are a distinct resource from known spells: the count scales by class level (a table), the list is chosen from all Druid spells for which you have slots, and the entire list can be swapped on a Long Rest. This is not a use_count, a known-cantrip pool, or a spell slot. It requires a new surface shape that captures: (a) count expression referencing a class-level table, (b) source = full class spell list filtered by available slots, (c) reset cadence = long_rest with full replacement.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Druid spell list. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Druid levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column. [...] Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells.
